steps.note: gcd(48, 36) by Euclid's rule: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b). Each step replaces the pair with (b, remainder) — always smaller, never losing the answer. When the remainder is 0, the other number is the gcd.
48 mod 36 = 12. Drop 48; carry (36, 12) to the next row.
36 mod 12 = 0. Drop 36; carry (12, 0) to the next row.
The remainder is 0, so the algorithm stops: gcd(48, 36) = 12. It took 2 division(s) — Euclid's method is logarithmic in the smaller number, not linear.
